title: He climbed to hide.
paragraphs: But Jesus called him down to be seen.
And that… is where everything broke open.
You don’t climb trees when your life is clean.
When you’re tired of being unseen… or worse—seen for all the wrong reasons.
He was small in the eyes of everyone who mattered.
A man who built wealth on other people’s wounds.
And the whispers followed him everywhere.

He had money—but no honor.
Power—but no peace.
A full house—but an empty soul.
So when he heard Jesus was passing by, something inside him snapped.
Running like a child through the streets.
Climbing a tree like his reputation didn’t matter anymore.
Because when your soul is starving, you stop protecting your image.
You just want to see Jesus.
But here’s the tension we don’t talk about:
Not to be known by Him.
He thought he could stay hidden.
Just one more curious observer in the crowd.
Just a sinner watching a Savior… from a distance.
We climb our own trees too.
We’re just not ready for Him to see everything.
The collision between hiding and holiness.
“Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today.” (Luke 19:5)
Grace didn’t wait for Zacchaeus to come down.
Some scholars interpret this moment as a public restoration—because in that culture, to dine with someone was to accept them fully.
Aligning Himself with the most rejected man in the city.
“He has gone in to be the guest of a man who is a sinner.” (Luke 19:7)
That’s always the accusation when grace shows up where people think it doesn’t belong.
But Jesus doesn’t operate on human approval.
And here’s where the story explodes.
No more branches to hide behind.
“Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor. And if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold.” (Luke 19:8)
No one told him to say that.
And suddenly greed loses its grip.
And repentance flows like a river.
Zacchaeus didn’t clean himself up to meet Jesus.
He changed because he met Jesus.
Sin is not just what you do.
And no amount of climbing—effort, religion, good works—can break that chain.
“For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.” (Luke 19:10)
Jesus didn’t pass through Jericho accidentally.
And He’s doing the same right now.
The one thinking, “If people really knew…”
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
But God didn’t wait for you to climb higher.
Lived the life you couldn’t live.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
On the cross, your sin was not ignored.
And three days later, Jesus rose again—proving that sin, shame, and death don’t get the final word.
Come down from “I’ll fix myself first.”
Because you don’t meet Jesus by climbing higher.
You meet Him by surrendering lower.
The places you said, “Not this, Lord.”
“Today salvation has come to this house.” (Luke 19:9)
Are you ready to come down?
